newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal PM Deuba loses crucial parliamentary vote.
newsitem.headline: Nepal PM Deuba loses crucial parliamentary vote.

text.p: Nepal's Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba lost a parliamentary vote of confidence on Thursday, officials said.

Deuba's 17-month-old coalition got 101 votes against a required minimum of 103 during voting on a motion he had moved to demonstrate the coalition's majority in the 205-seat lower house of parliament.
Officials said there were 92 votes against the confidence motion.
"Since the vote is inadequate the confidence motion has been rejected," said Ram Chandra Poudel, speaker of the House of Representatives, after announcing the results of the vote.
There was no immediate indication whether Deuba, whose three-party centre-right coalition has been beset by bitter feuds, would resign.
Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party, which has 87 seats, lost its majority last December following a split in the ranks of a partner, the Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), which had 19 seats.
